title: Governed native New Target command
intent: Complete the active B2 objective with a real create-to-Workbench path whose Target and immutable TargetRevision have one explicit authoritative writer.
scope: Add native Target and TargetRevision persistence, a versioned idempotent create command, Workspace and Project authorization, atomic audit and outbox facts, generated API contracts, and the flag-gated New Target experience without starting Temporal orchestration.
non_goals: Represent a native Target by silently creating a Case or Issue
Write native Target facts into compatibility projection tables
Introduce long-term dual write between Go and TypeScript
Start TargetWorkflow, RunWorkflow, Execution Gateway, or Runner migration
Enable the Verrail navigation flag globally
Commit, merge, deploy, or release without explicit approval
acceptance_criteria: One implementation is named as the sole authoritative writer for Target and TargetRevision and the choice is consistent with accepted ADRs.

A Workspace member with Project create authority can submit a strict New Target command with title, outcome owner, goal, constraints, acceptance criteria, risk, deadline, and applicable policy summary.
The command requires a bounded idempotency key and atomically persists the stable Target, immutable first TargetRevision, AuditEvent, and local outbox event.
Replaying the same key and payload returns the original result; reusing the key with a different payload fails with a stable conflict.
Workspace, Project, outcome-owner, and Principal boundaries fail closed without revealing inaccessible objects.
The create response returns opaque Target and TargetRevision IDs and the canonical Workbench can read the new native Target without using a Case or Issue surrogate.
The enabled shell exposes New Target from the confirmed global command and Project context, with accessible validation, pending, success, conflict, permission, and retryable failure states.
Compatibility projections and native Targets appear through one authorized read contract with unambiguous source and authority metadata.
Schema, API, idempotency, transaction rollback, authorization, audit, outbox, compatibility, UI, and browser tests pass with inspectable delivery evidence.
